Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Dermatitis of the hands/arms (likely irritant contact dermatitis with possible allergic contact dermatitis; potential atopic predisposition).
- Key findings supporting impression: Acute onset dry, itchy, red rash localized to exposed areas (hands/arms) after swimming; no fever or systemic symptoms; poor response to emollient (coconut butter); patient reports stress but otherwise well.
- Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  - Irritant contact dermatitis — High: Onset after swimming with involvement of exposed skin (hands/arms); dry, itchy, red skin; localized distribution; no systemic symptoms.
  - Allergic contact dermatitis — Medium: Possible exposure to pool chemicals, coconut butter, soaps/detergents; pruritic rash; temporal association with exposures.
  - Atopic dermatitis — Medium: Dry, itchy skin with potential atopic predisposition (family history of asthma and hayfever); hands/arms can be affected.
- Plan:
  - Topical corticosteroid cream to reduce inflammation.
  - Emollients to restore skin barrier; continue pasting onto affected areas as advised.
  - Over-the-counter oral antihistamines (e.g., Piriton or Loratadine) for itch as needed.
  - Paracetamol not indicated for this condition.
  - Avoid potential triggers (e.g., irritants/allergens) and monitor for response.
  - If symptoms persist or worsen after several days to a week, return for re-evaluation.
- Health Promotion & Planning:
  - Education on dermatitis management, skin hydration, and avoidance of irritants/allergens.
  - Health goals: reduction of itching and normalization of skin within days to a week.
  - Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.
  - Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Not recorded.
  - Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Return if not improving in 1 week.

  - Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management: Not required.

- Irritant contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Onset after swimming with exposure of exposed skin (hands/arms); dry, red, itchy skin; no systemic symptoms; localized distribution.
- Allergic contact dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Possible exposures to pool chemicals, coconut butter, soaps/detergents; pruritus with localized erythema.
- Atopic dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Dry, itchy skin with a positive family history of atopy (father with asthma, mother with hayfever); distribution on hands/arms can occur.
